equation_request.abstract: An important step in building a quantum computer is calibrating experimentally implemented quantum gates to produce operations that are close to ideal unitaries. The calibration step involves estimating the systematic errors in gates and then using controls to correct the implementation. Quantum process tomography is a standard technique for estimating these errors, but is both time consuming, (when one only wants to learn a few key parameters), and is usually inaccurate without resources like perfect state preparation and measurement, which might not be available. With the goal of efficiently and accurately estimating specific errors using minimal resources, we develop a parameter estimation technique, which can gauge key systematic parameters (specifically, amplitude and off-resonance errors) in a universal single-qubit gate-set with provable robustness and efficiency. In particular, our estimates achieve the optimal efficiency, Heisenberg scaling, and do so without entanglement and entirely within a single-qubit Hilbert space. Our main theorem making this possible is a robust version of the phase estimation procedure of Higgins et al. [11].

specification.problem: Estimate key systematic gate parameters (amplitude error and off-resonance error) of a universal single-qubit gate-set efficiently and robustly, using only single-qubit operations without entanglement, achieving Heisenberg scaling via a robust version of the Higgins et al. phase estimation procedure.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the robust phase-estimation-based calibration task for a single qubit; the circuits, the robustness proof, and the exact error model are not given in the abstract, so only a small illustrative finite instance is sketched.

equations.label: Heisenberg scaling
equations.description: Estimation error scales inversely with total number of gate applications, the optimal efficiency.
equations.abstract_quote: our estimates achieve the optimal efficiency, Heisenberg scaling
equations.justification: Heisenberg scaling means error ~ 1/resource; the exact constants are not given in the abstract.

equations.description: Applying a gate with a systematic rotation error k times amplifies the unknown angle to k\phi.
equations.justification: Standard model of phase-estimation-style amplification of a rotation angle; the actual gate model is not in the abstract.
assumptions: Error acts as coherent rotation about a fixed axis

steps.description: Apply the gate under test k times for k in an increasing sequence (e.g. powers of 2) so the error angle is amplified to k\phi.
Apply a basis-change rotation, then measure in the computational basis. Repeat for each k, with total gate count N to give 1/N error.

specification.measurement: Single-qubit computational-basis measurement after the k-fold gate and a basis-change rotation, repeated for several shots per k to estimate P(0|k) (and the orthogonal-quadrature probability).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate k\phi mod 2\pi from outcome frequencies for each k in the sequence, then combine across increasing k to refine \hat{\phi} (unwrapping the phase ambiguity); the robust estimator is not given in the abstract.
